why.question: Why strawberry, and why now?
why.request:
Why strawberry, and why now?
Answer in English, in at most three short sentences. Explain from this saved plan and its evidence; do not change any orders, context, or widgets. Focus on the highlighted cohort Low-price strawberry water ices, including what the weather-adjusted expectation does and does not explain.

response.reply:
Store replenishment requests for low-price strawberry water ices surged 44.6% above baseline over the past 14 days, accelerating even further recently across all retail stores. 

While seasonal heat lifts overall ice refreshment, weather-adjusted baseline models already account for typical temperature effects and cannot explain why this specific water-based cohort spiked while creamy strawberry items remained essentially flat (-0.6%). 

Because our records show no logged promotions or supplier shifts, a sustained shift in store demand mix is our current working interpretation, though the underlying driver remains unproven.

items.title: Are any store-level endcap displays or retail promotions planned for low-price strawberry water ices that would maintain demand above baseline through next month?
Should we plan promotional support or bundle pricing for chocolate-coated cones and bars to help clear stock as demand softens?

finding.district: HK Island, Kowloon, NT East, NT West
finding.explanation: Strawberry flavour triggered an earlier rise in HK Island, Kowloon, NT East, NT West (share 26.5% vs 23.3% expected) since 10 Jul. 20 of 20 stores show the change, and it is still there: last 7 days: units +18%; running for 22 days. A lasting change is one interpretation; these checks do not establish its cause. Descriptive breakdown: +1,743 units/week associated with the changed demand mix, +2,169 with overall demand. This arithmetic does not identify customer switching.
